Season Crop Report 2004-05

3.SOURCES OF IRRIGATION

Irrigation is the artificial application of water to the soil for growth of plants.

3.1 SOURCES OF IRRIGATION

Water is an important determinant factor of production of crops in agriculture sector. Intensive and extensive cultivation of land depend mainly on the availability of water. Medium and minor irrigation schemes are implemented in the state for augmenting the irrigation for agriculture. The various sources of irrigation are canals, tanks, tube wells, Open wells and springs. The number of sources of irrigation are furnished in the following table.

3.2 AREA IRRIGATED

The net area irrigated by different sources during 04-05 was 2637198 ha as against 2147673 ha in 03-04 showing an increase of 489525 ha or 22.8% over the previous year. The net area irrigated during 04-05 constituted 51.7% of the net area sown in the state. Villupuram district is at the top with 222021 ha Net area irrigated. However the highest percentage of the net area irrigated to the net area sown was recorded in Thiruvarur District with 96.4% followed by Kancheepuram District with 86.9% whereas the lowest percentage was recorded in The Nilgiris district with 0.9%. 3.2.1 CANALS (including System tanks)

Canals are the major source of irrigation in Tamilnadu. As the system tanks get supply from a permanent storage like reservoirs, dams etc. the area iirigated by this source is classified under canals. During 04-05, Canal irrigation accounted for 28.6% of the net area irrigated by all sources in the state. The net area irrigated by canals including system tanks during the year under review was 753819 ha as against 449458 ha in 03-04 recording an increase of 304361 ha i.e. 67.7%. The net area irrigated by canals is the highest in Thiruvarur district with 141206 ha (18.7%) followed by Thanjavur district with 131037 ha (17.4%) and Nagapattinam district with 118174 ha (15.7%) of the total net area irrigated by canals in the State.

3.2.2 TANKS (Non-Sysytem tanks only)

The non-system tanks which are fed partly from their independent catchment areas and partly from the diversion of river water and jungle streams depend fully on rain. The net area irrigated by non-system tanks during the year 04-05 is 4,65,355 ha as against 384960 ha in 03-04 registering an increase of 80395 ha or 20.9% over previous year. The extent of area irrigated by tanks during the year is the highest in Pudhukottai district with 15.3% followed by Sivagangai district with 14.5%, Ramanathapuram district with 13.2% and Kancheepuram district with 11.6%.

3.2.3 WELLS

Wells are the principal source of irrigation in Tamilnadu.During the year under review, open wells and tube-wells continued to be the principal sources of irrigation. The net area irrigated by openwells and tube-wells together accounted for 1400394 ha (about 53.1% of the total net area irrigated) in 04-05 as against 1298627 ha in 03-04 showing an increase of 101767 ha i.e. 7.8%. The net area irrigated by wells during the year 04-05 was the highest in Villupuram district with 12.1% of the total net area irrigated by the wells in the state followed by 9.1% in Thiruvannamalai district and 7.9% in Coimbatore district.

3.3 GROSS AREA IRRIGATED

Gross area irrigated includes the net area irrigated and the area irrigated more than once. Gross area irrigated by all sources during 04-05 is 3087108 ha as against 2478558 ha during 03-04 registering an increase of 608550 ha or 24.6 % over the previous year 03-04 due to better rainfall. The actual rainfall during the year 04-05 is 1078.8 m.m as against the normal rainfall of 961.9 m.m.

3.4 IRRIGATION INTENSITY

The irrigation intensity (The ratio of gross area irrigated to net area irrigated) is 1.17 for the state during 04-05. The ratio is significantly high in the districts of Kanyakumari (1.39), Vellore (1.38), Kancheepuram (1.31), Thiruvannamalai (1.31), Namakkal (1.29), Thiruvallur (1.24), Nagapattinam (1.24) and Thanjavur (1.22).
